tagline: A logging trail turned cattle road, under hundred-year-old oaks.
intro: Half an hour west of Stuart, County Road 714 runs 12 miles from Allapattah Road to State Road 710, and the locals call it simply the Grade. Cabbage palms, maples and hundred-year-old oaks arch over much of it, with pastures, groves, swamps and woods on either hand.
It began as a logging trail. In the early 1900s cowboys drove cattle along it, and citrus groves and ranches grew up beside it, with Lake Okeechobee off to the west.

moments.title: Allapattah Flats
moments.text: South of the road lies Allapattah Flats, what is left of the sloughs and wet prairies of the Alpatiokee Swamp in the northern Everglades.

moments.title: Indiantown
moments.text: Where the Grade meets Warfield Boulevard, the road runs on to Indiantown, an old Seminole trading post that S. Davies Warfield meant as a railroad's southern hub until the land boom fizzled.
